svg.text: The beat system — how a proactive line is decided, judged, and audited
Timers arm → gates filter → the ledger decides → a typed speak/hold → a second reading → ship with an audit row. Every knob is named beside the stage it controls.
All knobs live in the admin (Tuning → Engagement / Selling), take effect without a deploy, and are verified weekly by the conformance harness (docs/testing-flows.svg).
1 · Timers — when a beat may fire
In-panel follow-up ladder
Leads fast, backs off: 8s → 30s → 90s → 3m → 5m (last repeats).
Each rung's wait = base × dial (×1.5 while resting after holds).
Rung 1 is floored to reading time — ~300ms per word of the
newest reply (cap 90s) — never interrupt someone mid-paragraph.
nudge1Ms…nudge5Ms · assertiveness ×[1.5…0.65]
readFloorMs (the rung-1 reading floor)
Openers — the panel just opened
Peak attention, so the goal beat lands immediately: ~1.2s
signed-in · ~3s anonymous · ~1.1s returning to a live thread.
After a tapped bubble the ladder starts at the quick override.
A fresh open lets a still-fresh line stand (opener cooldown).
openerSignedMs · openerAnonMs · openerReengageMs
openerFollowMs · openerCooldownMs
Closed-panel re-engage bubble
Was active, went idle: after the idle threshold the server
composes one fresh line (or an explicit hold — then silence,
no canned fallback). Budgeted per audience; the bubble
withdraws itself if ignored.
reengageIdleAnonMs · reengageIdleSignedMs
reengageMaxAnon/Signed · bubbleWithdrawMs
2 · Client gates — a beat that fails one stays silent and names itself

g.text: quiet mode — a time-boxed pause, lifts by itself, on reload, or when they type (quietMs) · follow-up budget spent (nudgeCap) · too many unacknowledged
reach-outs — any sign of life resumes (unackedCap) · resting after consecutive holds (holdBudget, next try waits ×1.5) · the checkout sheet is open (sacred
ground) · anonymous visitor hasn't typed yet (by design) · the last word is the visitor's (reply, don't re-open) · a bubble is already on screen · post-sale
congrats grace, then the post-sale mode decides: upsell · presence · quiet (reengageGraceMs · reengagePostSaleWindowMs · postSaleMode)

svg.text: Every skip is observable: status().lastSkip names the gate with a timestamp; recentSkips keeps the last eight; nudgeArmedWhy shows the full arm arithmetic.
beat request → edge function (a context note — never logged as the shopper's words)
3 · The server decides — numbers first, model second
Repeat guards — vary the door, not the words
While ANY of the bot's own unprompted questions is unanswered → this beat is question-free.
From the 2nd reach-out on, each beat opens a new subject (read cross-surface + cross-conversation).
Reading the moment
Check-in #1 right after they spoke = a hot exchange, not idleness — but if the reply on screen runs past
80 words they're still reading: the brief demands one short fresh step or a hold, never stacked prose.
SALES LEDGER → ACTION TABLE (signed-in) — the beat's job is computed, not guessed
Ledger: orders by status · cloths already held · newest client-book facts · days since last order · anomalies · post-sale window · unmet goals · the 30-day spoken-action log.
Ordered rules pick ONE action: FIX_BLOCKED_ORDER → PROPOSE_COMPANION → PROPOSE_GIFT → ADVANCE_GOAL → KEEP_WARM → HOLD
An unanswered proposal rests on an escalating ladder — 24h → 3d → 7d — re-opened early by a new order or book note. KEEP_WARM gives one unasked piece of true house
expertise (once per section per day) before any silence. Briefs carry register colour: a colorway they do NOT yet have, the newest book facts — with the never-reveal reminder.
beats.ts · unit-tested on every deploy
substanceGate (the gate itself) · beat_actions (disable any rule per-key) · proposalRestHours (the rest ladder) · beat_notes (standing instructions on every brief)
Anonymous visitors (no register to compute from) fall back to the prompt's own judgment under the same guardrails. Every brief carries the full patron context —
customer block, client book, house instructions, goals for the section they're reading — plus the distilled house voice (the closed-panel bubble included).
4 · A typed decision — the model cannot leak a sentinel
Forced tool: beat_line {speak, line}
Speak/hold is a boolean field, not a magic word — the old [HOLD]
sentinel (and its decorated leaks) is structurally impossible.
Speech is the default posture; silence must be the honest last resort.
speak: true
speak: false → HOLD (audited, action not spent)
5 · The reach-out judge — a second, stricter reading before it ships
A pinned binary verdict (temperature 0, 4s timeout) vetoes only clear defects: leaked plumbing/meta ·
scorekeeping · invented commerce · pressure · broken output · inventorying the shopper's own data.
Fail-open: if the judge is unreachable the line ships — a quality gate is never an availability risk.
outreach.beatJudge (House rules, default on) · Haiku-class model
pass
veto
HOLD — silence as service
Nothing renders. Audited: a beat_hold row with the ledger
snapshot and the rule-by-rule trace — "why did it hold?" is a
lookup. A closed-panel HOLD short-circuits before the model call.
next try ×1.5 · rests after holdBudget consecutive holds
SPEAK — the line ships
1–2 plain sentences, every fact register-verbatim; on a buying
signal the commission button rides the same reply. Logged to
concierge_messages (bubble included) + a beat_action row.
nudgeCap · unacked until a sign of life · empty render withdrawn
VETO — killed
Stays silent. A beat_veto
row keeps the line + reason;
the action is NOT spent, so
the next beat may retry.
6 · The audit trail — every outcome leaves a row

g.text: Actions tab: the 7-day scoreboard — spoke · held · vetoed — each count filters the log; every row carries the ledger snapshot and decision trace.
Conversion tab: conversion by entry beat (typed / opener / nudge / tapped outreach) shows which beats actually sell; hold rate is the health guardrail.
Browser console: FeierabendConcierge.status() — lastSkip · recentSkips · nudgeArmedWhy (rung base × dial × spacious | floor | quick override) · reengage · postSale.
CI: beats.ts unit tests gate every deploy · the weekly conformance run proves each knob's live effect · the behavior deck and persona evals grade what the beats say.

svg.text: Beat trend in every deploy summary: this week's spoke/held vs last — drift is visible before it is a complaint.
7 · Where each knob lives — Tuning → Engagement (laid out as the visitor's journey) + Selling

g.text: ① Woven into the page — inline "Ask the mill" sections (inlineSections) · context chip budget (chipCap · chipLingerMs · chipRepeatMs) · ambient budget (maxAmbient)
② When the panel opens — the four opener timings · ③ A polite way out — the wrap chip (wrapChipMinTurns · wrapChipOnFollowup) · quiet window (quietMs)
④ While they read — the follow-up ladder, caps and budgets (nudge1–5Ms · nudgeCap · unackedCap · holdBudget) · re-engage thresholds and budgets (reengage*)
⑤ After they buy — grace, window + unit picker, mode (reengageGraceMs · reengagePostSaleWindowMs · postSaleMode) · proposal rest ladder (proposalRestHours)
House rules — substance gate · reach-out judge toggle · per-rule beat_actions · the written rules (engagement_base, versioned, "Load built-in to edit", History ⟲)
Tuning → Selling — how hard to sell (the dial scales ladder pace AND reach-out budgets) · selling method + worked examples (selling_base · exemplars_base, versioned + linted)
Everywhere: blank = built-in default · every save lands in concierge_edit_history (one-click rollback) · prompt-text saves get the advisory honesty lint · no deploy needed.

svg.text: The conformance harness reads these same keys and proves the live widget honors them — configured vs observed, weekly and on demand (docs/testing-flows.svg).
